name: Spot the gap
what_you_do: Find the one flaw in a candidate's framework: an overlap, a gap, or a bucket that doesn't belong.
how_it_helps: Interviewers judge your structure in the first two minutes; spotting weak frameworks fast keeps you from building one.

name: Fix the framework
skills: MECE structure, Case-specific structure, Structure depth
what_you_do: Fix a flawed framework so it's MECE and fits the case.
how_it_helps: Interviewers judge your structure in the first two minutes; this trains you to catch gaps before they do.

name: Framework builder
skills: MECE structure, Case-specific structure, Structure depth
what_you_do: Build your own framework for a case: 2–5 buckets, each with concrete sub-points.
how_it_helps: It's the first thing you say after the prompt; a tailored structure sets up the rest of the case.

name: Pick the best hypothesis
what_you_do: Pick the strongest starting hypothesis from four, given a few opening facts.
how_it_helps: Interviewers want a testable guess early, not a list of everything that could be wrong.

name: Fix the hypothesis
what_you_do: Rewrite a weak hypothesis so it names one cause, fits the facts and can be tested.
how_it_helps: A vague or overconfident hypothesis is a common early slip; a sharp one drives the whole analysis.

name: Initial hypothesis
skills: Forming a hypothesis, Updating a hypothesis
what_you_do: State a hypothesis and how you'd test it, then keep, revise or drop it when a new fact arrives.
how_it_helps: Interviewers hand you new data mid-case to see if you adapt instead of defending your first guess.

name: Setup only
what_you_do: Pick the right calculation for a business question, without solving it.
how_it_helps: Interviewers grade your setup first; a wrong setup sinks even perfect arithmetic.

name: Mental math
skills: Arithmetic, Zeros and units, Percentages, Growth
what_you_do: Solve quick percentages, growth and big-number problems in your head.
how_it_helps: Case math is done by hand under time pressure; speed and accuracy keep the case moving.

name: Consulting math
skills: Math setup, Arithmetic, Zeros and units
what_you_do: Set up and solve a two-step business word problem.
how_it_helps: Most case math looks like this: choose the formula, then get the number right.

name: Market sizing
skills: Sizing structure, Sizing assumptions, Arithmetic, Sanity checking
what_you_do: Size a market: pick the drivers, make assumptions, and sanity-check the result.
how_it_helps: Sizing questions test how you structure an unknown number; the logic counts as much as the answer.

name: Chart read
what_you_do: Pick the takeaway from a chart that matters most for the client.
how_it_helps: When you're handed an exhibit, the interviewer expects the 'so what' in seconds, not a tour of every bar.

name: Exhibit traps
what_you_do: Answer a question about a chart with one planted trap: units, axes, indexing or footnotes.
how_it_helps: Exhibits are often built to mislead; catching the trap is what separates strong candidates.

name: Needle in the table
what_you_do: Find the one or two numbers that matter in a dense table and do a quick calculation.
how_it_helps: Data-heavy exhibits test whether you can find what's relevant fast instead of reading everything.

name: Pick the best summary
skills: Answer first, Supporting evidence, Mid-case summary
what_you_do: Choose the best recommendation from four, given the case facts.
how_it_helps: The recommendation is what the interviewer remembers; this trains your ear for answer-first summaries.

name: Fix the recommendation
what_you_do: Rewrite a flawed recommendation so it leads with the answer and uses the right evidence.
how_it_helps: Burying the answer or citing the wrong facts is a common way to lose a strong case at the end.

name: 60-second recommendation
skills: Answer first, Supporting evidence, Complete recommendation
what_you_do: Write the recommendation you'd give in about 60 seconds, from a short fact sheet.
how_it_helps: Every case ends with 'so what should the client do?'; this is the closest drill to that moment.

name: What's next?
what_you_do: Pick the best next step, given where a case stands.
how_it_helps: Interviewers notice candidates who drive the case forward instead of waiting to be told what to do.

name: What do you need to know?
what_you_do: Say what data you'd ask for and where you'd start, in up to 60 words.
how_it_helps: Specific, prioritized requests show the interviewer you have a plan, not a wish list.
